issues.description: _BufferingHandler has unbounded memory growth with no size or time cap.
issues.detail: buffer: list[LogRecord] accumulates every root-logger record from _start_log_buffering until replay or cleanup, with no eviction. A slow-to-start session or chatty dependency can balloon memory and OOM the worker. Use a bounded deque or documented max-records/bytes cap to make the time semantics explicit.

issues.description: OTLP LoggingHandler is discovered by isinstance scan of root.handlers in multiple places.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry both walk logging.getLogger().handlers looking for LoggingHandler instances. This couples replay/shutdown to whatever happens to be attached to the root logger and breaks if a user installs their own OTel handler. _setup_cloud_tracer should return the handler instance and callers should track it by identity.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes all LoggingHandler instances from root, not just the one it installed.
issues.detail: The loop strips every opentelemetry LoggingHandler subclass from the root logger before force_flush. A user-installed OTLP LoggingHandler for their own pipeline gets silently detached. Track and remove only the specific handler instance installed by _setup_cloud_tracer.

issues.description: PR bundles unrelated changes: crash-log feature, worker.py race fix, and makefile/test removals.
issues.detail: The log buffering feature is mixed with a worker.py reorder of _pending_assignments before _queue_msg and a makefile change. Bundling makes review and bisection hostile. Split into separate commits or PRs so each change can be evaluated on its own rationale and risk.

issues.description: Removing -n auto and dropping test_plugin_google_stt.py from unit-tests is unexplained.
issues.detail: The diff serializes pytest (losing xdist parallelism) and silently excludes a plugin test file with no justification in the commit message. CI slows down and a test stops running. Either it is flaky (say so) or this is a debugging artifact that should be reverted.

issues.description: Bare except Exception in _on_cleanup swallows crash-log upload failures and drops the buffer.
issues.detail: The fallback init_recording call is wrapped in except Exception, then _stop_log_buffering discards buffered records. The whole point of the PR is troubleshooting; losing the buffer when upload fails defeats the goal. Narrow the exception and replay to stderr as a fallback.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR solves a real problem — capturing pre-session crash logs by buffering at the root logger and replaying into an OTLP handler — and that the core mechanism is sound. However, the implementation has consistent rigor issues: the buffer is unbounded, the OTLP handler is discovered by isinstance scan rather than tracked by identity, and shutdown removes handlers it does not own. The PR also bundles three unrelated changes (crash-log feature, worker.py race fix, makefile/test removals) that should be split. Verdict: needs work before landing — cap the buffer, return the handler as a value, narrow exceptions, and separate the unrelated changes.
